uncertain_points.claude: Agreed: crocodile-like snout, cone teeth, three-clawed strong arms, back sail, short hind legs (2014 study) and paddle-like tail (2020 study). Still debated: whether it walked on two legs or four on land (the 2014 study said four; studies in 2018, 2022 and 2024 favour two legs), whether the back structure was a thin sail or a fleshy hump, and whether it swam after prey or waded at the water's edge like a heron; a two-legged animal standing in shallow water is the safest picture.
uncertain_points.claude_brought_to_owner: Scientists agree on the crocodile-like snout, the sail, the short back legs and the paddle tail. uncertain_points.claude: Only one incomplete skeleton is known, and its limbs and shoulder and hip bones are missing, so the flippers are drawn from related elasmosaurs. Length figures differ: Wikipedia gives about 10.3 m with a 7.1 m neck, while older figures of 13 to 14 m (Cope's 13.7 m; 42 ft quoted in the 2013 PLOS ONE paper) still circulate. Studies also give a wide range for how far the neck could bend (about 75 to 177 degrees), but agree it could not hold a swan pose.
